options.text: Yes — the metal strip is a conductor, so it completes the current path and the lamp can glow.
No — a metal strip across the gap blocks the current path, so the lamp stays dark.
Yes — the lamp glows even if the gap is left open, because the cell is still in the circuit.
No — the lamp glows only if two metal strips are placed in the gap.

stem:
The diagram shows Qasim's circuit: a cell, a lamp, and a gap. A metal strip (a conductor) closes the gap so a current path can form.

Will the lamp glow?

teacher.key_rationale: A metal conductor across the gap closes the circuit so current can pass and the lamp can glow.
teacher.figure_note: Cell, lamp, and metal strip closing the test gap.
